front: OSPFv3 for IPv6 uses which Next Header number?
back: 89, directly over IPv6 rather than TCP or UDP.

front: OSPFv3 multicast groups on an ordinary IPv6 link?
back: ff02::5 AllSPFRouters; ff02::6 AllDRouters. They have link-local scope.

front: Source address of an OSPFv3 Hello on an ordinary link?
back: The sending interface's link-local address. ff02::5 is the multicast destination.

front: Must OSPFv3 neighbors have the same global IPv6 prefix?
back: No. They communicate per link using link-local addressing; still verify the intended global addressing and client path.

front: OSPFv3 router ID size and format?
back: 32 bits, dotted decimal, such as 1.1.1.1. It is not a 128-bit IPv6 next-hop address.

front: No IPv4 addresses and no explicit RID on classic IOS OSPFv3?
back: The process can fail to obtain a RID. Configure a unique router-id explicitly.

front: Normal IOS broadcast/point-to-point OSPFv3 Hello and dead defaults?
back: 10 seconds and 40 seconds. Compare effective timers after any configuration changes.

front: Which OSPFv3 identifier distinguishes instances on the same link?
back: The instance ID; it must agree for the intended relationship. Classic IPv6-unicast syntax uses instance 0 by default.

front: Does the local OSPFv3 process number have to match the neighbor?
back: No. It is local configuration, unlike the area and compatible on-link instance ID.

front: Classic command to activate OSPFv3 process 10 in area 0?
back: ipv6 ospf 10 area 0 under the interface. It is not an IPv4-style network statement.

front: What distinguishes the address-family interface activation from classic ipv6 ospf?
back: Address-family style uses ospfv3 PROCESS ipv6 area AREA. Match the command family to the supported process configuration; do not mix forms blindly.

front: Meaning of O and [110/11] in show ipv6 route?
back: O is an intra-area OSPF route here; 110 is administrative distance, 11 is metric. Interpret the next hop with its exit interface.

front: Normal OSPFv3 advertisement of an interface in Loopback state?
back: A global address is represented as a /128 host prefix, even if its address command has /64. Verify the actual advertised route.

front: Does OSPFv3 preempt an existing DR when a higher-priority router joins?
back: No. It retains the OSPF election and non-preemption principles used in OSPFv2.

front: What does Interface ID mean in show ipv6 ospf neighbor?
back: The neighbor's interface identifier. The final Interface column names the local interface.

front: OSPFv3 repeatedly in ExStart/Exchange: what should you compare?
back: MTUs and database-exchange evidence, along with the intended link parameters. Do not bypass MTU checking as the first repair.

front: What does a controlled OSPFv3 process restart do to adjacencies?
back: It drops the local process adjacencies and can apply a pending RID change. It does not guarantee a fresh segment-wide DR election.

front: Does a passive OSPFv3 LAN still need interface activation?
back: Yes. Passive suppresses neighbor formation; activation is needed to advertise its connected prefix.

front: Is the dotted-decimal OSPFv3 router ID its IPv6 next-hop address?
back: No. The RID identifies the OSPF speaker; forwarding commonly uses its link-local address and the local exit interface.

front: Does an OSPFv3 Full neighbor prove the intended global LAN prefix is correct?
back: No. Check the actual LAN address, its activation and the learned prefix. Link-local adjacency can work despite a global addressing-plan error.
